segments.title: Groundwork for the new route handlers and service functions
context: This change adds an API that lists, reads, creates, updates and deletes Pokemon, and asks for the same API key as the trainer API. A request that names a Pokemon or a trainer that does not exist gets a 404, and a create request with an unknown type, the same type twice, an empty name or a level outside 1 to 100 gets a 422.

waypoints.title: Added the set of the 18 Pokemon types
waypoints.reading: The author added a constant `POKEMON_TYPES` that holds the 18 type names in lower case. [`check_known_type()` looks each type of a create request up in it](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L19), so a create request with the type `"thunder"` gets a 422.

waypoints.title: Added `PokemonCreate` for the body of a create request
waypoints.reading:
The author added a pydantic model `PokemonCreate` that:

- requires a `name` of 1 to 40 characters and a `primary_type`
- sets `level` to `5` when the body leaves it out, and requires 1 to 100 otherwise
- sets `secondary_type` and `trainer_id` to `None` when the body leaves them out
- raises `ValueError` from `check_known_type()` and `check_types_differ()` for a wrong type

[`add_pokemon()` takes its body as a `PokemonCreate`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/routes.py#L21), so FastAPI returns a 422 for a body that breaks one of these rules, before [`create_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#create_pokemon) runs.
waypoints.coreChange: This is the contract of `POST /api/pokemon`: every body passes these rules before [`create_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#create_pokemon) writes a row, and the two new tests check two of them.

children.title: Added the `name` field with a length of 1 to 40
children.reading: The author added a field `name` that takes a text of 1 to 40 characters. A longer name gets a 422, so every name fits [the `String(40)` column of `Pokemon`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/models.py#L11).

children.title: Added the `level` field with a range of 1 to 100
children.reading: The author added a field `level` that takes a whole number from 1 to 100, and is `5` when the body leaves it out. [A new test sends a level of 101 and expects a 422](code:tests/test_pokemon.py#L14-16).

children.title: Added the two type fields and the `trainer_id` field
children.reading: The author added a required `primary_type`, and a `secondary_type` and a `trainer_id` that are `None` by default. [`create_pokemon()` loads the trainer when `trainer_id` is set](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L25-26), so a new Pokemon never names a trainer that does not exist.

waypoints.title: Added a validator that raises `ValueError` for an unknown type
waypoints.reading: The author added a field validator `check_known_type()` that raises `ValueError` for a `primary_type` or a `secondary_type` that is not in [`POKEMON_TYPES`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#POKEMON_TYPES). It returns `None` unchanged, so a body with no `secondary_type` passes. Pydantic turns the error into a 422, so [a body with the type `"thunder"`](code:tests/test_pokemon.py#L9-11) gets a 422 and no row is written.

waypoints.title: Added a validator that raises `ValueError` for the same type twice
waypoints.reading: The author added a model validator `check_types_differ()` that raises `ValueError` when `primary_type` and `secondary_type` are the same. It runs after the field validators, because of `mode="after"`, so it compares two known types. A body with `"fire"` as both types gets a 422.

waypoints.title: Added `PokemonUpdate` for the body of an update request
waypoints.reading: The author added a pydantic model `PokemonUpdate` with [the five fields of `PokemonCreate`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L10-14), each `None` by default. [`update_pokemon()` dumps it with `exclude_unset=True`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L36), so a PATCH changes only the fields its body names. It keeps the length of `name` and the range of `level`, and has no validator for the types.

findings.title: `PokemonUpdate` lets a PATCH store a type outside `POKEMON_TYPES`
findings.reading: [`PokemonUpdate` declares `primary_type` and `secondary_type` as `str | None`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L33-34), with no copy of [`check_known_type()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L16-21). [`update_pokemon()` copies every set field onto the row](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L39-40), so a PATCH stores a type that a POST gets a 422 for.
trace: [`edit_pokemon(1, PokemonUpdate(primary_type="thunder"))`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/routes.py#L26-27) runs, because no validator of `PokemonUpdate` raises.

[`setattr(pokemon, "primary_type", "thunder")`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L40), then [`session.commit()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L41) stores it, and the response is a 200 with `"primary_type": "thunder"`.

findings.title: `PokemonUpdate` passes `null` to columns that are `NOT NULL`
findings.reading: [`name`, `level` and `primary_type` take `None`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L31-33), and a body that sets one of them to `null` keeps it in [`model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L36). [The matching columns of `Pokemon` are `Mapped[str]` and `Mapped[int]`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/models.py#L11-13), which SQLAlchemy creates as `NOT NULL`. So [`session.commit()` raises `IntegrityError`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L41), and the client gets a 500 in place of a 422.
trace: [`session.commit()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L41) raises `IntegrityError: NOT NULL constraint failed: pokemon.name`, and FastAPI returns a 500.

children.title: Added an optional `name` field with a length of 1 to 40
children.reading: The author added a field `name` that is `None` by default, and takes a text of 1 to 40 characters when it is set, as [`PokemonCreate.name`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L10) does.

children.title: Added an optional `level` field with a range of 1 to 100
children.reading: The author added a field `level` that is `None` by default, and takes a whole number from 1 to 100 when it is set, as [`PokemonCreate.level`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L11) does. A PATCH with a level of 101 gets a 422.

children.title: Added the optional type fields and the `trainer_id` field
children.reading: The author added `primary_type`, `secondary_type` and `trainer_id`, each `None` by default. [`update_pokemon()` loads the trainer](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L37-38) when `trainer_id` is set to a number. The two type fields take any text.

waypoints.title: Added `PokemonRead` for the body of every response
waypoints.reading: The author added a pydantic model `PokemonRead` with [the six columns of `Pokemon`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/models.py#L10-15). Every handler of the router that returns a body names it in `response_model`, as [`read_pokemon()` does](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/routes.py#L15), so FastAPI returns these six fields and no other attribute of the row.

children.title: Added `from_attributes` to read a `Pokemon` row
children.reading: The author set `from_attributes=True`, so pydantic reads the fields from the attributes of [the `Pokemon` row that `find_pokemon()` returns](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L21), in place of the keys of a `dict`.

children.title: Added the six fields of the response
children.reading: The author added `id`, `name`, `level`, `primary_type`, `secondary_type` and `trainer_id`, with the types of [the matching columns of `Pokemon`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/models.py#L10-15). `secondary_type` and `trainer_id` are `None` when the row has no value.

waypoints.title: Added two tests that send a create request with a wrong field
waypoints.reading:
The author added a test file that sends `POST /api/pokemon/` with the API key from `API_KEY`, and:

- `test_add_pokemon_rejects_an_unknown_type()` sends the type `"thunder"`, which [`check_known_type()` raises `ValueError` for](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L19-20), and expects a 422
- `test_add_pokemon_rejects_a_level_above_100()` sends a level of 101, which [the range of `PokemonCreate.level`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L11) does not take, and expects a 422

Both stop at [`PokemonCreate`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#PokemonCreate), so neither test reads or writes the database.

waypoints.title: Added the include of the Pokemon router under `/api`
waypoints.reading: The author added a call to `app.include_router()` that puts `/api` before every route of [`pokemon_router`](code:src/pokedex/main.py#L6), and adds `Depends(verify_api_key)` to each of them. [`verify_api_key()` raises a 401 for a wrong `x-api-key` header](code:src/pokedex/security.py#L8-10), so the Pokemon routes ask for the same key as [the trainer routes](code:src/pokedex/main.py#L15).

waypoints.title: Added the `Pokemon` model for the `pokemon` table
waypoints.reading: The author added a SQLAlchemy model `Pokemon` on [`Base`](code:src/pokedex/database.py#L13-14) that maps the `pokemon` table. [`create_pokemon()` builds one from the body of a create request](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L27), and [`PokemonRead` reads its attributes](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L39) for every response.

children.title: Added the table name `pokemon`
children.reading: The author set `__tablename__` to `"pokemon"`, so SQLAlchemy reads and writes the `pokemon` table.

children.title: Added the `id` primary key
children.reading: The author added an `id` column as the primary key. The database sets it on insert, and [`find_pokemon()` loads a row by it](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L18).

children.title: Added the `name` column of up to 40 characters
children.reading: The author added a `name` column of type `String(40)` that is `NOT NULL`. Its length is the length that [`PokemonCreate.name`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L10) takes.

children.title: Added the `level` column
children.reading: The author added a `level` column of whole numbers that is `NOT NULL`. The column has no range: [`PokemonCreate.level`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L11) keeps the value from 1 to 100.

children.title: Added the `primary_type` column of up to 10 characters
children.reading: The author added a `primary_type` column of type `String(10)` that is `NOT NULL`. The longest names in [`POKEMON_TYPES`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#POKEMON_TYPES), `"electric"` and `"fighting"`, have eight characters, so every known type fits.

children.title: Added the nullable `secondary_type` column
children.reading: The author added a `secondary_type` column of type `String(10)`. Its annotation is `Mapped[str | None]`, so the column is `NULL` for a Pokemon with one type.

children.title: Added the `trainer_id` foreign key to `trainers.id`
children.reading: The author added a nullable `trainer_id` column with a foreign key to `trainers.id`. [`list_pokemon()` filters on it](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L13), so `GET /api/pokemon?trainer_id=1` returns the Pokemon of trainer 1.

waypoints.title: Added the Pokemon router with the prefix `/pokemon`
waypoints.reading: The author added an `APIRouter` with the prefix `/pokemon` and the tag `pokemon`. [`main.py` includes it under `/api`](code:src/pokedex/main.py#L16), so the five handlers of this file answer at `/api/pokemon` and `/api/pokemon/{pokemon_id}`.

waypoints.title: Added `read_all_pokemon()` for `GET /api/pokemon`
waypoints.reading: The author added a route handler `read_all_pokemon()` that returns [`list_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#list_pokemon) as a list of [`PokemonRead`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#PokemonRead). FastAPI reads `trainer_id` from the query string, so `GET /api/pokemon?trainer_id=1` returns the Pokemon of trainer 1 and `GET /api/pokemon` returns all of them.

waypoints.title: Added `read_pokemon()` for `GET /api/pokemon/{pokemon_id}`
waypoints.reading: The author added a route handler `read_pokemon()` that returns the Pokemon that [`find_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#find_pokemon) loads. For an id with no row, `find_pokemon()` raises `NotFoundError`, and [`not_found_handler()` returns a 404](code:src/pokedex/errors.py#L11-12) with `"pokemon 7 not found"`.

waypoints.title: Added `add_pokemon()` for `POST /api/pokemon`
waypoints.reading: The author added a route handler `add_pokemon()` that passes the parsed [`PokemonCreate`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#PokemonCreate) body to [`create_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#create_pokemon), and returns the new Pokemon with a 201. A body that breaks a rule of `PokemonCreate` gets a 422 before the handler runs, which [the two new tests](code:tests/test_pokemon.py#L9-16) check.

waypoints.title: Added `edit_pokemon()` for `PATCH /api/pokemon/{pokemon_id}`
waypoints.reading: The author added a route handler `edit_pokemon()` that passes the id and the [`PokemonUpdate`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#PokemonUpdate) body to [`update_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#update_pokemon), and returns the updated Pokemon. It answers `PATCH`, so a client sends only the fields it changes.

waypoints.title: Added `remove_pokemon()` for `DELETE /api/pokemon/{pokemon_id}`
waypoints.reading: The author added a route handler `remove_pokemon()` that calls [`delete_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#delete_pokemon) and returns a 204 with no body. For an id with no row, `delete_pokemon()` raises `NotFoundError`, so the client gets a 404.

waypoints.title: Added `list_pokemon()` to load the Pokemon, sorted by name
waypoints.reading: The author added a function `list_pokemon()` that selects every `Pokemon` ordered by `name`, and adds `WHERE trainer_id = …` when `trainer_id` is not `None`. [`read_all_pokemon()` returns its list](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/routes.py#L12) as the body of `GET /api/pokemon`.

waypoints.title: Added `find_pokemon()` to load one Pokemon or raise `NotFoundError`
waypoints.reading: The author added a function `find_pokemon()` that loads a row by its primary key with `session.get()`, and raises `NotFoundError("pokemon", pokemon_id)` when there is none. [`read_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/routes.py#L17), [`update_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L35) and [`delete_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L47) call it, so all three return a 404 for an unknown id through [`not_found_handler()`](code:src/pokedex/errors.py#L11-12).

waypoints.title: Added `create_pokemon()` to insert a new Pokemon
waypoints.reading:
The author added a function `create_pokemon()` that:

- raises `NotFoundError` through [`find_trainer()`](code:src/pokedex/trainers/service.py#L13-17) when the body names a trainer that does not exist
- builds a `Pokemon` from every field of the body
- inserts the row, commits, and reloads it, so `id` is set

[`add_pokemon()` returns the reloaded row](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/routes.py#L22) as the body of the 201.

children.title: Added a trainer check before the insert
children.reading: The author added a condition that calls `find_trainer()` when `trainer_id` is set. [`find_trainer()` raises `NotFoundError("trainer", trainer_id)`](code:src/pokedex/trainers/service.py#L15-16) for a trainer that does not exist, so the request gets a 404 and no row is inserted.

children.title: Added the new `Pokemon` row built from the body
children.reading: The author added a `Pokemon` built from `draft.model_dump()`, so each field of [`PokemonCreate`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L10-14) sets the column of the same name on [`Pokemon`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/models.py#L10-15).

children.title: Added the new row to the session
children.reading: The author added `session.add(pokemon)`, which puts the new row in the session. Nothing is written to the database yet, so [the commit](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L29) on the next line inserts it.

children.title: Added the commit of the insert
children.reading: The author added `session.commit()`, which writes the new row to the `pokemon` table, so the row is in the database before [`add_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/routes.py#L22) returns the 201.

children.title: Added a refresh that reloads the new row
children.reading: The author added `session.refresh(pokemon)`, which reads the row back from the database after the commit. The row then has the `id` the database gave it, so [`add_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/routes.py#L22) returns that `id` in the body of the 201.

waypoints.title: Added `update_pokemon()` to write the changed fields onto a Pokemon
waypoints.reading:
The author added a function `update_pokemon()` that:

- loads the Pokemon with `find_pokemon()`, which raises `NotFoundError` for an unknown id
- keeps only the fields the body sets, with `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`
- raises `NotFoundError` through [`find_trainer()`](code:src/pokedex/trainers/service.py#L13-17) when the body sets a trainer that does not exist
- copies each kept field onto the row, then commits and reloads it

[`edit_pokemon()` returns the reloaded row](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/routes.py#L27), so a PATCH with `{"level": 12}` changes the level and nothing else.
waypoints.coreChange: This is the only code that changes a stored Pokemon: every field a PATCH body sets is copied onto the row here, so the fields of [`PokemonUpdate`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#PokemonUpdate) decide what an update can write.

children.title: Added the lookup of the stored Pokemon
children.reading: The author added a call to [`find_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#find_pokemon) that loads the row of `pokemon_id`, so a PATCH of an unknown id gets a 404 before any field is read.

children.title: Added the dump of the fields the body sets
children.reading: The author added `changes.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`, which leaves out every field the body does not name. A body of `{"level": 12}` gives `{"level": 12}`, so [the loop](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L39-40) changes only `level`.

children.title: Added a trainer check before the update
children.reading: The author added a condition that calls [`find_trainer()`](code:src/pokedex/trainers/service.py#L13-17) when the body sets `trainer_id` to a number. A `trainer_id` of `null` skips the call, so a PATCH can set the trainer of a Pokemon to `None`.

children.title: Added a loop that copies each kept field onto the row
children.reading: The author added a loop that calls `setattr(pokemon, name, value)` for each entry of `fields`, so each field of [`PokemonUpdate`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/schemas.py#L31-35) writes the column of the same name on [`Pokemon`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/models.py#L10-15).

children.title: Added the commit of the changed fields
children.reading: The author added `session.commit()`, which writes the fields that [the loop](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#L39-40) copied onto the row, so a PATCH with `{"level": 12}` stores the new level.

children.title: Added a refresh that reloads the updated row
children.reading: The author added `session.refresh(pokemon)`, which reads the row back from the database after the commit, so [`edit_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/routes.py#L27) returns the stored value of every field.

waypoints.title: Added `delete_pokemon()` to delete a stored Pokemon
waypoints.reading: The author added a function `delete_pokemon()` that loads the row with [`find_pokemon()`](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/service.py#find_pokemon), deletes it and commits. [`remove_pokemon()` calls it](code:src/pokedex/pokemon/routes.py#L32), so a DELETE of an unknown id gets a 404 and a DELETE of a stored id gets a 204.
